message.content: {"predictors": [{"name": "Inventory Growth", "construction": "Calculate the year-over-year percentage change in inventories from Compustat annual data: (Inventories_t - Inventories_{t-1}) / Inventories_{t-1}.", "rationale": "Rising inventories may signal slowing demand or over-optimism by management, while shrinking inventories may reflect strong sales or conservative management.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}, {"name": "Short-Term Debt to Total Assets", "construction": "Divide short-term debt (Compustat: Debt in Current Liabilities) by total assets, measured at fiscal year-end.", "rationale": "Firms with higher reliance on short-term debt may face refinancing risk and financial distress, while low ratios indicate stability.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}, {"name": "Receivables to Sales Ratio", "construction": "Compute accounts receivable (Compustat) divided by net sales (Compustat) for the most recent fiscal year.", "rationale": "A high ratio could point to aggressive revenue recognition or deteriorating customer quality.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}, {"name": "R&D Intensity Change", "construction": "Calculate the annual change in R&D expenditure-to-sales ratio: (R&D_t / Sales_t) - (R&D_{t-1} / Sales_{t-1}).", "rationale": "Rising R&D intensity may signal increased investment in future growth opportunities.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Dividend Deviation", "construction": "Take the absolute difference between the most recent annual dividend and the three-year average dividend, divided by the three-year average dividend.", "rationale": "Unusually large changes in dividend policy may indicate information about future prospects or risk.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}, {"name": "Cash Flow Skewness", "construction": "Compute the skewness of quarterly operating cash flows over the past three years (12 quarters) for each firm.", "rationale": "Firms with large positive or negative skew in cash flows may be subject to unusual events or earnings management.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}, {"name": "Gross Margin Expansion", "construction": "The change in gross margin (gross profit divided by sales) from the prior fiscal year to the current year.", "rationale": "Improving gross margins may indicate strengthening competitive position or operational efficiency.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "SG&A to Sales Decline", "construction": "Measure the year-over-year change in SG&A expense divided by sales, using Compustat annual data.", "rationale": "Firms that are effectively controlling overhead (declining SG&A/Sales) may achieve higher profitability.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}, {"name": "Net Insider Buying", "construction": "Sum net insider purchases (Form 4 filings, SEC) over the past 12 months, scaled by shares outstanding.", "rationale": "Insider buying may reflect superior private information regarding firm prospects.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Sales Volatility", "construction": "Compute the standard deviation of quarterly sales growth rates over the past three years (12 quarters).", "rationale": "High sales volatility may indicate unpredictable fundamentals and higher risk.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}]}
